jobs.description:
Maintenance Supervisor Laramie, Wyoming
About Us Tungsten Parts Wyoming (TPW) is a small business in Laramie, WY and a major supplier of custom tungsten fragments for the defense industry.
TPW specializes in the precision production of high-performance tungsten components. Our manufacturing operation runs 24/7/365 and is built to meet demanding defense-industry requirements. We produce tungsten balls, spheres, and cubes with a focus on safety, quality, consistency, and precision.
Job Description Job Type: Benefited full-time; in person
Work Location: Laramie, WY
The Maintenance Supervisor is responsible for keeping TPW's production equipment, furnaces, and facilities running safely and reliably in a 24/7/365 manufacturing environment. This position owns the preventive maintenance schedule, leads maintenance activities on complex furnaces and production machinery, coordinates outside subcontractors, and supports facility maintenance and planning operations across the site.
The ideal candidate has hands-on maintenance experience in a production environment, strong planning and organizational skills, good judgment around safety, and the ability to work effectively with operators, supervisors, and outside vendors.
Work Environment Includes • On-the-job training
• Growth opportunities
• Company perks
• 24/7/365 manufacturing environment
• Work around furnaces, machine tools, and production equipment
Responsibilities • Build, maintain, and execute the preventive maintenance schedule for production equipment, furnaces, and facility systems.
• Perform and lead maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair on complex furnaces and production machinery.
• Plan maintenance windows to minimize disruption to production sequencing and throughput.
• Source, schedule, and supervise subcontractors for specialized repairs, installations, and facility work.
• Support facility maintenance and planning operations, including building systems, utilities, and site infrastructure.
• Maintain maintenance logs, equipment records, and documentation in their entirety.
• Manage spare parts, consumables, and maintenance supplies.
• Communicate equipment status, downtime risks, and repair needs to production leadership.
• Enforce safety procedures, including lockout/tagout, during all maintenance activities.
• Support continuous improvement in equipment reliability and uptime.
• Be able to lift up to 50 pounds when needed.
Qualifications • Must be 18 years or older.
• Hands-on maintenance experience required; production or manufacturing environment experience ideal.
• Experience maintaining furnaces, ovens, or comparable thermal processing equipment preferred.
• Experience coordinating and working with subcontractors and outside vendors.
• Strong mechanical and troubleshooting skills across mechanical, electrical, and facility systems.
• Able to plan, prioritize, and document maintenance work.
• Strong communication skills and ability to work with a team.
• Must be able to stand for extended periods of time.
• Must pass background check.
• Must be a U.S. Citizen.
Benefits & Pay • Competitive supervisor-level pay, based on experience
• 401(k) with up to 6% company match
• Holiday pay
• Dental insurance
• Health insurance
• Life insurance
• Paid time off
• Referral bonus program
• Vision insurance
Schedule • Full-time
• Primarily day shift
• On-call and after-hours response as required to support the 24/7/365 operation
Employment Eligibility In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.

About Greystar

Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit www.greystar.com.

Job Description Summary

This role oversees and performs technical and mechanical work that ensures the inside and external buildings, ground, amenities, and common areas of the community meet the Company’s standards for cleanliness, appearance, safety, and overall functionality.

Job Description

Assists and completes work orders generated from resident requests for service, as well as routine upkeep on the community by diagnosing the source or cause of the defect or problem, and making repairs in accordance with established policies, procedures, safety standards, and code requirements.
Oversees and completes the “make-ready” process to prepare vacant apartment homes for leasing and new move-ins by completing the pre-move-out inspection, creating a “punch” list of maintenance work needed, scheduling vendors and contractors as needed, obtaining needed supplies and materials, completing all maintenance tasks, and inspecting completed work.
Develops standards for the cleanliness and overall appearance of the community’s grounds, amenities, building exteriors, market ready unit interiors, breezeways, curbs, signage, leasing office, central garbage areas, parking lots, and other buildings and common areas to ensure that they reflect and represent the high quality of the community and Greystar standards.
Periodically inspects work performed by other service team members to assess effectiveness of policies and procedures and develop corrective action plans as needed.
Periodically inspects work performed by contractors, vendors and other service providers to verify the work, materials and services meet quality standards, scope and specifications as required.
Maintains adequate inventory of spare parts and maintenance materials and works with Community Manager to order supplies and tools as needed to stay within budgetary guidelines.
Completes monthly preventative maintenance procedures as outlined in the Policy and Procedure Manual.
Assists Community Manager in developing the budget for regular repair and maintenance and capital projects.
Supports cost-cutting and expense control programs by fixing rather than replacing parts when possible, not being wasteful with materials and supplies, and practicing the correct use for tools and equipment.
Conducts regularly scheduled Greystar safety meetings, ensure all MSDS sheets are current and readily accessible, and keeps up to date on all OSHA and other safety related laws and requirements to ensure community compliance.
Demonstrates customer services skills by treating residents and others with respect, answering questions from team and residents, responding sensitively to complaints about maintenance services, and assigned work orders with efficiency and urgency.

BASIC KNOWLEDGE & QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma, GED, or related experience and training.
Experience in property management maintenance, other building maintenance, or related trade.
Incumbents must provide own hand tools unless prohibited by State law and must be knowledgeable and skilled in the safe use and maintenance of hand tools, power tools, user-moved aids, mechanical equipment and measuring devices.
Ability to apply principles of logical thinking to define and correct problems.
Proficiency in customer service and interpersonal communication skills in order to effectively interact with residents, clients, team members, and other business contacts, respond courteously to questions and requests, and stay calm when addressing and resolving customer problems.
Ability to read, write, and communicate effectively to represent company management in a support capacity, act as the first point of contact for internal team members and external visitors to the Company, and answer questions related to department operating policies.
Proficiency in internet, word processing, spreadsheet, and database management programs in order to maintain records of information and develop and provide information for the manager’s use. Property management system experience preferred.
Mathematical skills necessary to add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers, decimals, and fractions in order to review and complete various financial, administrative, and legal documents.

SPECIALIZED SKILLS:

Incumbents must have EPA certifications Type I and II or Universal if the position requires working on a sealed HVAC system to test system pressures, handle refrigerants, etc.
Incumbents must have all certifications as required by State and Local jurisdictions.
Incumbents must have a valid driver’s license to operate a golf cart on the property, if applicable.

TRAVEL / PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Incumbents need to be able to stand, walk, and/or sit for extended periods of time and bend, stoop, climb ladders, reach, carry objects, and crawl in confined areas.
Incumbents must be able to work inside and outside in all weather conditions (rain, snow, heat, hail, wind, sleet).
Job demands may require incumbents to push, pull, lift, carry, or maneuver weights of up to twenty-five (25) pounds independently and fifty (50) pounds with assistance.
Local, routine travel may be required to attend business meetings, training programs, or other situations necessary for the accomplishment of some or all of the daily responsibilities of this position.
Incumbents must be able to work a flexible work schedule, which includes taking “call” during evenings, weekends, and holidays.

The hourly range for this job is $30 - #31.

:

Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Leadership Development Programs Manager

The Real Estate Council

Reports to the Senior Director TREC

Leadership is a core competency of The Real Estate Council. It is essential to the long-term sustainability of our industry and our community that we provide programs and services that assist in talent recruitment and retention for our member companies. Our purpose is to provide connections that impact careers, companies, and communities. 

Position

The Leadership Development Programs Manager manages TREC’s leadership development programs and committees, including the Associate Leadership Council (ALC), Young Guns Core Committee, Leadership Alumni, Mentorship Program, and DEI Leadership Committee. This role serves as the primary staff liaison to volunteer leaders and advances TREC’s leadership strategy through programming, member engagement, and volunteer management.

The Manager oversees planning, recruitment, budgets, and evaluation while strengthening TREC’s leadership continuum and member experience. Working across departments, the role ensures initiatives align with organizational goals and develop future industry and community leaders.

Competencies

Achievement focus: Demonstrates persistence and overcomes obstacles. Measures self against standard of excellence. Recognizes and acts on opportunities.
Communications: Superior written and oral communication skills. Keeps others adequately informed. Must be confident, articulate and poised with the ability to represent the executives at meetings in their absence.
Cost conscious: Conserves organizational resources, contributes to profits and revenue through implementation of cost savings measures and working within the approved budget.
Leadership: Exhibits confidence in self and others. Inspires respect and trust. Motivates others to perform well. Reacts well under pressure. Positive attitude with great attention to detail, follow-through, ability to prioritize tasks, work independently, and juggle multiple priorities in fast-paced environment.
Dependability : Attendance and punctuality. Some early morning and late evenings required, primarily driven by timing of events and class or committee functions.
Job Knowledge : Experienced fundraiser including donor cultivation, solicitations, and donation mechanisms.
Planning and Organization: Willingness to make decisions, integrates effective change, uses resources effectively, and includes appropriate people in decision-making process.
Project Management: Communicates change and progress, completes projects in a timely manner and within budget and looks for ways to improve and promote quality.
Quality: Fosters quality focus in others, measures key outcomes, sets clear quality requirements, solicits, and applies stakeholder feedback.
Creative thinker- constantly thinking of programs and ways to inspire our members and TREC team to help them develop their leadership skills at all levels.
Physical Requirements : Requires prolonged standing, prolonged stationary position, frequent walking or movement, and the ability to lift objects weighing up to 20 lbs.

Essential Functions

Manage and provide strategic oversight for TREC’s Leadership Development initiatives, ensuring alignment with the organization’s mission, priorities, and member needs. Serve as primary staff liaison for ALC, Young Guns Core Committee, Leadership Alumni, Mentorship Program, DEI Leadership Committee, and related initiatives.

Lead planning, execution, evaluation, and improvement of leadership programs that strengthen engagement, cultivate leaders, and enhance TREC membership value. Partner with volunteers to set goals, develop programming, recruit participants, and measure outcomes.

Identify opportunities to expand TREC’s leadership continuum and create meaningful pathways for members at every career stage. Build relationships with members, volunteers, industry leaders, and community stakeholders to advance participation and organizational objectives.

Exercise sound judgment and initiative in managing programs, volunteers, budgets, and priorities. Maintain professionalism, organization, and clear communication while collaborating with staff, board members, volunteers, and partners to deliver an excellent member and volunteer experience.

Skill Requirements

Proficiency in Microsoft 365, Salesforce/CRM database management (Nimble), and Adobe Creative Suite. Excellent organizational, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

Special Requirements

Local travel, evening, and some weekend work required. Must have a current driver’s license, reliable transportation, and the ability to set up and run meetings and events, including meeting related physical demands.

Bachelor’s degree required.
1–3 years of experience in program management, leadership development, volunteer management, membership organizations, nonprofit associations, corporate training, talent development, or related field.
Demonstrated experience managing committees, volunteer leaders, boards, or advisory groups.
Experience developing, planning, and executing educational, leadership development, or professional development programs and events.
Ability to build relationships with executive-level professionals, volunteers, sponsors, and community leaders.
Experience with managing budgets, tracking program performance, and evaluating outcomes.
Strong project management skills and ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders.
Experience with membership databases, CRM systems, and event registration platforms preferred (Nimble AMS/Salesforce experience a plus).
Knowledge of commercial real estate, workforce development, leadership development, or association management preferred.

Strengthen TREC’s leadership continuum and create pathways for member engagement and growth.
Establish annual goals, performance measures, and success metrics for leadership development programs and committees.

Provider and Referral Development

Build and maintain relationships with pediatricians, diagnosticians, psychologists, schools, daycares, speech and occupational therapy providers, hospitals, social workers, case managers, and community organizations.

Develop new referral partnerships while strengthening relationships with existing partners.
Serve as a reliable point of contact between Blossom and professional referral sources.

Community Outreach

Represent Blossom at local conferences, networking events, school programs, resource fairs, and community events.
Identify partnership opportunities that improve access to ABA therapy and other resources for families.
Coordinate targeted outreach initiatives with the Director of Marketing and state leadership.
Deliver approved marketing and referral materials to priority organizations.
Help strengthen Blossom’s visibility and professional reputation throughout the assigned market.

Referral Growth and Follow-Up

Generate qualified patient referrals from professional and community relationships.
Maintain a structured follow-up schedule with referral partners.
Track which organizations are referring, which relationships require additional development, and where new opportunities exist.
Communicate referral updates appropriately and help create a responsive experience for professional partners.
Work with intake and operations teams to identify and address referral-process barriers.
Support referred families without making clinical promises or guarantees regarding insurance authorization, staffing, or start dates.

CRM and Performance Reporting

Record contacts, visits, calls, emails, meetings, events, referrals, and follow-up activities in CRM.
Maintain accurate referral-source and professional-contact information.
Use platform to plan routes and document field visits.
Provide weekly updates on outreach activity, developing partnerships, referrals, pipeline movement, and market opportunities.
Use CRM data to determine which relationships and territories are producing meaningful results.
Track qualified referrals based on families reaching Pending Initial Authorization or a later client-pipeline stage.
Track Active Clients separately as the final conversion outcome.

New qualified professional contacts established
In-person provider visits and meetings completed
Follow-up activities completed on time
New referral partnerships developed
Professional referrals generated
Referrals reaching Pending Initial Authorization or later
Referrals progressing to assessment and active services
Accuracy and consistency of CRM documentation
Growth within assigned territories and priority referral accounts

At least two years of experience in healthcare business development, provider relations, referral development, community outreach, outside sales, account management, or a related position.

Already understands healthcare referral relationships

Is comfortable walking into offices and initiating conversations
Follows up consistently without damaging the relationship
Can balance compassionate communication with measurable growth expectations
Uses data and CRM activity to guide their work

Competitive base salary based on relevant experience

Health and additional benefits according to company eligibility
Professional development and advancement opportunities

About HPD, The Office Of Housing Access And Stability

The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) is the nation’s largest municipal housing preservation and development agency. Its mission is to promote quality and affordability in the city's housing, and diversity and strength in the city’s neighborhoods because every New Yorker deserves a safe, affordable place to live in a neighborhood they love.

The Office of Housing Access and Stability (“HAS”) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunity, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. The mission of the office is to ensure fair, efficient, and transparent access to affordable housing. The Office provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.

Your Team

At HPD, rent subsidy programs are administered by the Division of Tenant & Owner Resources (DTOR). HPD’s rental subsidies, including Section 8 or the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program, provide funding to eligible low-income families for rental assistance toward decent, safe, and affordable housing in a neighborhood of their choice. Families pay approximately 30% of their income toward rent, and the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) pays the difference, directly to the owner. The unit must have a rent that is determined reasonable and affordable by HPD and must meet federal Housing Quality Standards (HQS) to be approved.

Your Impact

HPD's Division of Tenant & Owner Resources (DTOR) is responsible for the administration of rental subsidy programs that include Housing Choice Voucher (HCV), Project Based Voucher (PBV), Moderate Rehab Section 8, Moderate Rehab Single Room Occupancy (SRO), and Continuum of Care (CoC)-Shelter Plus Care (SPC) and NYC 15/15. Through these programs, HPD serves over 40,000 households and 9,000 landlords in all five boroughs. DTOR is responsible for the initial application screening; confirming eligibility requirements; briefing applicants; and issuing vouchers. DTOR also monitors tenant and landlord compliance of their obligations under each program and continues to administer the ongoing subsidies throughout their participation. These continued activities include processing annual and interim recertifications to update family income/assets, household composition, and rent amounts; tenant moves and transfers; approved rent increases; Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) abatements and reinstatements to enforce Housing Quality Standard (HQS) inspection results; and providing customer service to stakeholders through our Client Services office, call center and the DTR Portal.

Your Role

All Case Managers in the Division of Tenant and Owner Resources are expected to perform case management functions to provide necessary and important services to assist and expedite Section 8 vouchers to HPD clients. These services may consist of meeting with groups in-house, attending workshops or attending community events. Case managers are also expected to participate in tenant activity programs and projects to coordinate functions that aim to improve tenant-management relations, as well as encourage participation related to Section 8 dealings. Additionally, Case managers will ensure participant cases are accurately screened and reviewed for completeness and in compliance with Federal HUD Rules and Regulations.

Key Responsibilities

Manage a caseload of assisted or applicant households
Initial voucher application screening
Determination and verification of eligibility
Client briefings (internal and external meetings)
May perform community outreach to assist Section 8 participation
Prepare and send appropriate correspondence, track responses

Demonstrate ability to manage multiple cases while prioritizing cases for processing
Attend mandatory trainings

Excellent Communication Skills (both orally and in writing)
Strong Customer Service Focus
Computer Proficiency
Bilingual a Plus
Section 8 or other Rental Subsidy experience a Plus

Authorization to work in the United States is required for this position. The NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development does not provide sponsorship for international employees for visa applications, extensions, or status changes, including H-1B visas. New qualified professional contacts established

Professional referrals generated

Referrals progressing to assessment and active services

Growth within assigned territories and priority referral accounts

Uses data and CRM activity to guide their work

About HPD, The Office Of Housing Access And Stability

The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) is the nation’s largest municipal housing preservation and development agency. Its mission is to promote quality and affordability in the city's housing, and diversity and strength in the city’s neighborhoods because every New Yorker deserves a safe, affordable place to live in a neighborhood they love.

The Office of Housing Access and Stability (“HAS”) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunity, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. The mission of the office is to ensure fair, efficient, and transparent access to affordable housing. The Office provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.

Your Team

At HPD, rent subsidy programs are administered by the Division of Tenant & Owner Resources (DTOR). HPD’s rental subsidies, including Section 8 or the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program, provide funding to eligible low-income families for rental assistance toward decent, safe, and affordable housing in a neighborhood of their choice. Families pay approximately 30% of their income toward rent, and the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) pays the difference, directly to the owner. The unit must have a rent that is determined reasonable and affordable by HPD and must meet federal Housing Quality Standards (HQS) to be approved.

Your Impact

HPD's Division of Tenant & Owner Resources (DTOR) is responsible for the administration of rental subsidy programs that include Housing Choice Voucher (HCV), Project Based Voucher (PBV), Moderate Rehab Section 8, Moderate Rehab Single Room Occupancy (SRO), and Continuum of Care (CoC)-Shelter Plus Care (SPC) and NYC 15/15. Through these programs, HPD serves over 40,000 households and 9,000 landlords in all five boroughs. DTOR is responsible for the initial application screening; confirming eligibility requirements; briefing applicants; and issuing vouchers. DTOR also monitors tenant and landlord compliance of their obligations under each program and continues to administer the ongoing subsidies throughout their participation. These continued activities include processing annual and interim recertifications to update family income/assets, household composition, and rent amounts; tenant moves and transfers; approved rent increases; Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) abatements and reinstatements to enforce Housing Quality Standard (HQS) inspection results; and providing customer service to stakeholders through our Client Services office, call center and the DTR Portal.

Your Role

All Case Managers in the Division of Tenant and Owner Resources are expected to perform case management functions to provide necessary and important services to assist and expedite Section 8 vouchers to HPD clients. These services may consist of meeting with groups in-house, attending workshops or attending community events. Case managers are also expected to participate in tenant activity programs and projects to coordinate functions that aim to improve tenant-management relations, as well as encourage participation related to Section 8 dealings. Additionally, Case managers will ensure participant cases are accurately screened and reviewed for completeness and in compliance with Federal HUD Rules and Regulations.

Manage a caseload of assisted or applicant households
Initial voucher application screening
Determination and verification of eligibility
Client briefings (internal and external meetings)
May perform community outreach to assist Section 8 participation
Prepare and send appropriate correspondence, track responses

Demonstrate ability to manage multiple cases while prioritizing cases for processing
Attend mandatory trainings

Excellent Communication Skills (both orally and in writing)
Strong Customer Service Focus
Computer Proficiency
Bilingual a Plus
Section 8 or other Rental Subsidy experience a Plus

The NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development does not provide sponsorship for international employees for visa applications, extensions, or status changes, including H-1B visas. Company Description

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation committed to advancing security of energy supply, economic growth and environmental sustainability through energy policy co-operation. The IEA operates as an autonomous body within the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. Both the OECD and the IEA seek opportunities to work with an increasing number of non-members of growing importance to the world economy. The Agency aims to foster the contribution of the energy sector to economic development and environmental sustainability across the globe.

The IEA sub-Saharan Africa Programme has been expanding over the past few years, with a rising number of IEA analyses and reports, with deeper relations and collaboration with governments and energy stakeholders from the continent, including through both high- and technical-level events involving participants from sub-Saharan African or held in sub-Saharan African. Four countries in sub-Saharan African are part of the IEA family as Association countries: Kenya, Nigeria, Senegal, and South Africa.

The core missions of the IEA sub-Saharan African Programme include leading the IEA’s institutional engagement with sub-Saharan African counterparts—with a strong focus on Association countries—coordinating cross-agency work on sub-Saharan Africa, and delivering specific publications and projects. Support with analytical work, both qualitative and quantitative, peer review of IEA reports with a focus on sub-Saharan Africa and collaborate with other IEA teams to incorporate sub-Saharan African perspectives and sensitivities into IEA analytical outputs.
Contribute to the communication efforts of the IEA and the sub-Saharan Africa Programme, including
